prune.description: destroy this scene's previously-applied actors that are no longer in the spec (tag-scoped; never touches hand-placed actors)

spec_json.description: the spec as inline JSON text (alternative to spec_path)

spec_path.description: path to a unreal.scene/v1 JSON spec file

tools.name: scene_apply

tools.description: Remove all actors a given scene_id previously applied (tag-scoped; leaves hand-placed actors untouched).

scene_id.description: the scene id whose actors to remove

tools.name: scene_clear

tools.description: Render a target (or the whole level) from N orbit angles into one contact-sheet montage — a quick multi-angle visual of a level/asset for design validation. Editor world (backgrounded-safe).

elevation.description: camera elevation degrees above horizon; default 25 (0 = horizontal orbit)

fill.description: fraction of the frame the target fills; default 0.7

fov.description: vertical field of view degrees; default 60

target.description: actor labels/globs to frame; empty = whole level

tools.name: scene_contact_sheet

tools.description: Deterministic quantize+SHA1 hash over actor OR HISM/ISM instance transforms — the authored-content oracle (verify a map hashes to an expected value; instance-aware where level_diff is not).

limit.description: instances scope: max instances to hash; default 5,000,000 (raise for a huge HISM city)

pos_bucket.description: position quantization in world units; default 1

tools.name: scene_digest

tools.description: Compile a scene spec and diff it against the current level (add/update/prune, missing asset refs) WITHOUT mutating — a dry run to review before scene_apply.
tools.name: scene_plan

tools.description: Reposition existing actors to their snapshot transforms (undo a move/rotate/scale experiment). Transform-only: it does NOT recreate actors deleted since the snapshot or remove ones spawned since (delete those with delete_actor / pie_destroy). Reports labels no longer present.
tools.name: scene_restore

tools.description: Save the current level's actor transforms (by label) to a named snapshot file so a MOVE/rotate/scale experiment can be undone with scene_restore. Scope is transforms only — it does not record spawns/deletes.

class_filter.description: only snapshot actors matching this class/label substring

tools.name: scene_snapshot

tools.description: Capture the actual display as a PNG — the whole virtual desktop (all monitors), one monitor, or a region. This is an OS screenshot of what is really on screen (unlike take_screenshot, which renders the 3D scene inside the editor). Downscaled to max_width for token economy.

max_width.description: downscale so the image is at most this many px wide (aspect preserved); default 1600, 0 = full resolution

monitor.description: monitor index (0-based, see list from MonitorRects); omit or -1 = whole virtual desktop spanning all monitors

region.description: [x,y,w,h] in virtual-desktop pixels to grab a sub-rectangle instead of a whole monitor

tools.name: screen_capture

tools.description: Set the editor selection by actor labels (mode replace|add|remove|none), optionally framing the result.

frame.description: frame the selection in the viewport after selecting

tools.name: select_actors

tools.description: Move/rotate/scale an actor by label. Each of location [x,y,z], rotation_pyr [pitch,yaw,roll], scale [x,y,z] is optional.
tools.name: set_actor_transform

tools.description: Set the project's default GameMode in DefaultEngine.ini (offline, idempotent).
tools.name: set_gamemode

tools.description: Register a HUD WidgetBlueprint to auto-appear when the game starts (PIE/editor-gated, cvar-guarded, cooked-safe) — so an authored HUD shows in-game without a project HUD convention. The shipped path is assign_subclass into the project's own HUD property.

hud_widget.description: the HUD WidgetBlueprint class to auto-spawn

tools.name: set_hud_widget

tools.description: Set the player input mode (GameOnly / GameAndUI / UIOnly) and cursor visibility — required to make a menu interactive (UIOnly + cursor) and to hand control back to gameplay (GameOnly).
tools.name: set_input_mode

tools.description: Set the current level's WorldSettings GameMode override (a per-map override; use set_gamemode for the project default).
tools.name: set_world_gamemode

tools.description: Spawn an actor in the current level from a native class or Blueprint asset path.

class_path.description: native class (/Script/Engine.PointLight) or Blueprint asset path (/Game/BP_Thing); for a mesh prop use /Script/Engine.StaticMeshActor + static_mesh_path

z.description: Z location; defaults to 100 when omitted

tools.name: spawn_actor

tools.description: Start a play-in-editor session in the current level. simulate=true runs the world without possessing a player.

simulate.description: run the world without possessing a player pawn

tools.name: start_play

tools.description: Stop the current play-in-editor session.
tools.name: stop_play

tools.description: Run the style cohesion Layer-A deterministic audit (readonly) against captured frame paths.
tools.name: style_cohesion

tools.description: Render the scene and return it as a PNG image. Uses a synchronous scene capture so it works even when the editor is backgrounded (editor world only, not during PIE).
tools.name: take_screenshot

tools.description: Type a literal Unicode string at the OS level into the focused control (KEYEVENTF_UNICODE — layout-independent). Use for search boxes, names, and paths; use key_press for shortcuts and navigation keys.

text.description: the literal text to type as Unicode characters

tools.name: type_text

tools.description: Click a live UMG widget by name or viewport coordinate via the Slate pointer path (works on a backgrounded editor; needs a realized painted window — returns SLATE_WINDOW_UNAVAILABLE under headless -nullrhi). Returns the target widget's own state delta; verify downstream effects with a follow-up widget_read.

coord.description: [x,y] viewport coordinate to click instead of a named widget

tools.name: ui_click

tools.description: Run the verb response Layer-A deterministic audit (readonly) against an input burst and envelope.
tools.name: verb_response

tools.description: Get the editor viewport camera pose (and game-view state where available). Feeds camera framing for capture.
tools.name: viewport_get

tools.description: Control the editor viewport: move the camera to a pose, pilot/eject an actor, toggle game view, or run viewport console commands. Returns the resulting camera pose.

camera_location.description: [x,y,z] to move the editor viewport camera to

console.description: console commands to run against the viewport (e.g. 'r.ScreenPercentage 100')

game_view.description: toggle Game View (hides editor-only actors); like pressing G

pilot_actor.description: actor label to pilot the viewport camera with

tools.name: viewport_set

tools.description: Bind a UMCPButton's OnClicked to a named command (Resume/Quit/OpenPanel) — a persisted node property consumed at runtime, no graph authoring. Discover commands via widget_describe. Fails WIDGET_NOT_MCPBUTTON on a plain Button.

command.description: a RunNamedCommand name discovered via widget_describe (Resume/Quit/OpenPanel)

tools.name: widget_bind_event

tools.description: Configure a live gameplay data binding on a UMCPHUDWidget: a target widget field (ProgressBar.Percent, TextBlock.Text) pulls from a gameplay source (owning_pawn/pc/player_state/world_actor/ability_system) each tick, with an optional conversion (ratio for health, format_text for ammo, int_to_text, bool_to_visibility). Validates the path at author time (BIND_PATH_UNRESOLVED).

max_path.description: denominator path for conversion=ratio, e.g. MaxHealth

path.description: dotted source path, e.g. Health or HealthComponent.Health

target_field.description: its field, e.g. Percent or Text

target_widget.description: the widget to drive, e.g. HealthBar

tools.name: widget_bind_field

tools.description: Add MVVM view bindings (widget property <- viewmodel field, with an optional conversion) to a WidgetBlueprint. Fails BIND_TYPE_MISMATCH with the compile log on an unbindable type pair. Spike-gated.
tools.name: widget_bind_mvvm

tools.description: Render a WidgetBlueprint OFFSCREEN at one or more resolutions (no PIE, no foreground) and return per-resolution geometry and/or pixels — the multi-resolution layout oracle (assert anchored elements stay pinned + inside the SafeZone across 720p/1080p/4K) and the golden-image source for image_compare. Geometry inside an embedded composite is opaque (capture the child WBP standalone).

geometry.description: return per-widget on-screen rects (works headless via a layout-only pass)

pixels.description: export a PNG per resolution (needs an active RHI; RHI_UNAVAILABLE under -nullrhi)

warmup_frames.description: frames to render before reading (warms fonts/materials); default 3

tools.name: widget_capture

tools.description: Compile a WidgetBlueprint and return the structured compiler log (errors/warnings) + digest. Terminates a deferred widget_compose transaction. Fails BINDWIDGET_UNSATISFIED with the log if a required bound widget is missing.
tools.name: widget_compile

tools.description: THE primary UMG authoring verb: apply a declarative nested widget tree to a WidgetBlueprint — add/update/reorder/reparent nodes, set slots/props/brush/font, embed composite sub-widgets — then compile once (atomic). Convergent + idempotent: re-composing the same tree yields the same digest. Returns the read-back tree + digest + compile_log (+ a restore_token for destructive changes).

blueprint.description: the WidgetBlueprint asset path to compose into

defer.description: patch mode: keep the transaction open (mutations apply but do NOT compile) until an explicit widget_compile

mode.description: full (default): reconcile the whole tree (convergent — any starting tree yields the spec). patch: update only the given nodes, leaving others

prune.description: remove any existing node absent from the spec (destructive; snapshotted). Default false = additive

remove.description: node names to remove (snapshotted first; returns a restore_token)

tree.description: declarative nested widget node: {name, class, slot?, props?, brush?, font?, is_variable?, children?[]}. class is a friendly name (TextBlock/ProgressBar/Image/Button/CanvasPanel/VerticalBox/Overlay/…) or a /Script or /Game path; a /Game WBP or UserWidget subclass is embedded as ONE opaque composite node (its subtree is not expanded). Every node MUST be named. slot is slot-class-aware (CanvasPanelSlot: anchor_preset|anchors+offsets+alignment+z; BoxSlot: size+padding+align; GridSlot: row/col/span)

tools.name: widget_compose

tools.description: Create a WidgetBlueprint (UMG HUD/menu) asset. Defaults to a plain UserWidget with a CanvasPanel root. Returns the root name + any required BindWidget slots. Then author the tree with widget_compose.

parent_class.description: parent UserWidget class; default /Script/UMG.UserWidget. Use the plugin UMCPHUDWidget ONLY for a gameplay-bound HUD (widget_bind_field/track_actor) — it adds a plugin parent-class dependency you MUST bake out before shipping

root_panel.description: root panel widget class; default CanvasPanel (use Overlay for a stacked full-screen menu)

tools.name: widget_create

tools.description: Describe the authorable UMG palette, or one widget class: its editable props, its slot class (what layout body its children take), and — for UMCPHUDWidget — its BindWidget requirements + named-command handlers. Plan authoring against this instead of guessing class/prop names.

widget_class.description: a widget class to describe — its editable props, slot class, and (for UMCPHUDWidget) its BindWidget requirements + named-command handlers. Omit for the full authorable palette (panels + leaves)

tools.name: widget_describe

tools.description: Read a LIVE widget's runtime state in the current viewport: per node name/class/visible/text/percent/checked/enabled + on-screen geometry (current viewport only — for multi-resolution geometry use widget_capture). discover:true enumerates on-screen widgets the project itself created (not just bridge-shown ones).

discover.description: enumerate on-screen widgets the project created (not just bridge-shown ones)

handle.description: a live widget handle; omit with discover:true to enumerate on-screen widgets

include_geometry.description: include current-viewport on-screen rects (painted widgets only)

tools.name: widget_inspect

tools.description: Build the one UI material a render-target minimap needs: an MD_UI material sampling a SceneCapture render target, a dynamic instance, applied to a minimap Image brush. The last mile that makes a world-render minimap fully buildable.

image_widget.description: a minimap Image node to apply the material to

render_target.description: the SceneCapture TextureRenderTarget2D asset path to sample

tools.name: widget_make_rt_material

tools.description: Fast single value read from a live widget (a named sub-widget's field, e.g. ProgressBar.Percent) — the predicate source for pie_verify. Works by name; no is_variable needed.

field.description: the field/property to read (e.g. Percent, Text); default a sensible per-class value

tools.name: widget_read

tools.description: Render a UserWidget class (e.g. /Script/PolyWorld.CityBuildWidget) OFFSCREEN to a PNG at out_path (width x height) via FWidgetRenderer — no PIE. The UMG HUD visual-iteration loop.
tools.name: widget_render

tools.description: Push values into a live (shown) widget in one round-trip: set named fields (health Percent, ammo Text, visibility) via the UMCPHUDWidget setters — which force a Slate refresh so the on-screen widget actually updates — and/or invoke named UFUNCTIONs. Partial-failure: per-entry issues. (A UUserWidget is not an actor, so pie_set_property/pie_exec can't reach it — this is the driver.)

fields.description: [{widget_name, field, value}] — pushed via the typed setter matching value's type, with a forced Slate refresh

handle.description: a live widget handle from widget_view show

tools.name: widget_set_fields

tools.description: Set keyboard/gamepad focus on a named sub-widget of a live widget — pairs with a pie_input Up/Down/Accept nav nudge to verify controller/keyboard-navigable menus (not just mouse clicks).
tools.name: widget_set_focus

tools.description: Configure a marker widget to track a world actor: each tick it projects the actor's world location to DPI-correct widget space and positions the marker (forced point-anchor + centered pivot). The objective-marker binding — a configured property, no graph authoring.

marker_widget.description: the marker widget to reposition each tick

target.description: world-actor label to track, or owning_pawn

world_offset.description: [x,y,z] world-space offset from the actor origin

tools.name: widget_track_actor

tools.description: Inspect or restore a WidgetBlueprint's widget tree. mode=get returns the canonical tree JSON + structural digest (the layer-1 oracle, no rendering). mode=restore re-applies a snapshot from a restore_token.

mode.description: get (default): read the current in-memory tree + structural digest. restore: re-apply a snapshot

restore_token.description: restore mode: the token returned by a prior destructive widget_compose

tools.name: widget_tree

tools.description: Show or hide a WidgetBlueprint in the running (PIE) viewport. show returns a handle to drive/observe it; hide releases it. The viewport keeps a shown widget alive (no manual rooting); keep_alive holds it across a hide/re-show.

blueprint.description: show: the WidgetBlueprint to instantiate + add to the viewport

handle.description: hide: the handle returned by a prior show

keep_alive.description: show: hold a strong ref (C++ UPROPERTY) so the handle survives a hide/re-show

owner.description: show: owning player-controller actor label (default the first local PC)

tools.name: widget_view

tools.description: Author a UMVVMViewModelBase Blueprint with typed FieldNotify properties (the MVVM data source). Spike-gated: falls back to the UMCPHUDWidget push/pull path if MVVM authoring is intractable in this UE version.
tools.name: widget_viewmodel_create

tools.description: Capture a specific on-screen window as a PNG — defaults to auto-detecting the Unreal Editor. Sees the FULL editor: menus, panels, the Content Browser, modal dialogs, the composited viewport with UI. method=print (default) works even when the window is backgrounded/occluded and does not steal focus; method=screen blits its on-screen rectangle. Returns the window's screen bounds so you can map image pixels to mouse_control coordinates.

focus.description: bring the window to the foreground before capturing

hwnd.description: target an exact window handle (from list_windows)

max_width.description: downscale to at most this width; default 1600, 0 = full resolution

method.description: auto|print|screen. print (default) renders the window even when backgrounded/occluded and never steals focus; screen blits its on-screen rectangle (window must be visible)

pid.description: target a specific process id instead of by title

title.description: window title substring (case-insensitive); omit to auto-detect the Unreal Editor

tools.name: window_capture

tools.description: Spatial verification in the game world (PIE): line_trace (is a shot/LOS clear?), sphere_overlap (what's near a point?), nav_path (can AI path A->B?), project_point (is a point on the navmesh?). Needs collision + a built navmesh.

world.description: auto|editor|game; default auto (game world in PIE)

tools.name: world_query
